name: scikit-learn
summary: A Python machine-learning library organized around cloneable estimator objects, fit/transform/predict protocols, compositional meta-estimators, and cross-validated model selection.

features.name: Cloneable estimator protocol
features.description: BaseEstimator derives parameter names from explicit constructor arguments, exposes get_params and set_params, and supports cloning constructor state without fitted attributes. Estimators learn data-dependent state in fit and expose learned attributes with a trailing underscore.
benefits: Gives tools a uniform way to inspect, configure, and reproduce estimators
costs: Constructor signatures become part of interoperability requirements
Estimator authors must respect fit/reset and parameter identity conventions

features.name: Fit, transform, and predict contracts
features.description: The developer API distinguishes estimators that fit state, transformers that preserve sample correspondence while changing features, predictors that produce outputs, and models that score data. Pipeline validates these capabilities by position in a sequence.
benefits: Allows heterogeneous algorithms to participate in shared workflows
Makes training and inference stages explicit
costs: Interface conformance does not guarantee statistical correctness
Data validation and feature-shape compatibility remain runtime concerns

features.name: Pipeline and meta-estimator composition
features.description: Pipeline chains named transformers and a final estimator, forwards nested parameters with name__parameter keys, and can cache fitted transformers. GridSearchCV wraps an estimator, clones candidates, evaluates parameter settings under cross-validation, and can refit the selected configuration.
benefits: Encodes preprocessing and prediction as one configurable object
Supports systematic parameter search without hand-written orchestration
costs: Nested cloning and fitting can multiply memory and compute use
Pipeline correctness depends on ordering, leakage control, and compatible interfaces

features.name: Validation and capability metadata
features.description: Scikit-learn validation utilities establish input and fitted-state checks, while estimator tags describe capabilities such as supported inputs, outputs, and methods for generic checks and dispatch.
benefits: Enables common checks and conditional behavior across estimator families
Surfaces input-shape and capability assumptions programmatically
costs: Tags and validation add protocol surface to every estimator
Capability metadata may depend on parameters or runtime environment

mathematical_views.question: Which objects can be composed when they share fit, transform, predict, parameter, and fitted-state contracts?
assumptions: Objects are modeled by supported methods and parameter behavior rather than inheritance alone
fit creates state that later methods consume
The view abstracts individual statistical algorithms

mathematical_views.question: How do named meta-estimator components expose and update parameters recursively?
assumptions: Nodes are estimators or transformers and edges are named containment relations
The __ separator provides a path encoding for nested parameters
Setting parameters preserves the component graph unless a whole step is replaced

mathematical_views.question: How does parameter search map candidate estimator states to validation scores and a refitted choice?
assumptions: Each candidate is cloned before fitting
Splits and scoring define the evaluation relation
A selected candidate is not a proof of generalization outside the sampled protocol

mathematical_views.question: What state transition distinguishes an unfitted estimator from one ready for prediction or transformation?
assumptions: fit is the transition that creates learned attributes
Trailing-underscore attributes represent learned state by convention
Repeated fit replaces prior learned state except documented warm-start behavior

costs: Strict constructor and state conventions constrain implementation style
Runtime validation cannot capture every semantic incompatibility

benefits: Reusable workflow composition and automated search
costs: Nested fits, cloning, and cross-validation can be computationally expensive

benefits: Generic tooling can adapt to declared capabilities
costs: Metadata and validation paths increase framework surface area
